grounding.derivation: This is a composed interface responsibility grounded in the implementation, not an external protocol assertion: handlePrepare explicitly puts inst.vbal in PrepareReply.VBallot while keeping joined inst.bal separately; handlePrepareReply requires the latter for attempt qualification and compares the former to select prior command/attributes/status. Transport must deliver the reported value context unchanged for that consumer meaning. Neither the same-ballot guard nor the independent local self-reply behavior defines a conversion of remote VBallot to zero. New/Unmarshal on the actual network path provides no reconstruction. The requirement is message fidelity, not eventual selection of every reported value.
grounding.applicability: Applies to a successful codec round trip of the actual handlePrepare response under complete byte delivery. Fixed check uses a real producer prefix; sockets, asynchronous scheduling and scanner trigger are outside this local responsibility.
alternatives: A zero-valued input will agree with a zero-initialized decoded field; this does not establish preservation of nonzero values.

func (t *PrepareReply) Marshal(wire io.Writer) {
	var b [18]byte
	var bs []byte
	bs = b[:17]
	tmp32 := t.AcceptorId
	bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Replica
	bs[4] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[5] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[6] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[7] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Instance
	bs[8] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[9] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[10] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[11] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Ballot
	bs[12] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[13] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[14] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[15] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	bs[16] = byte(t.Status)
	wire.Write(bs)
	bs = b[:]
	alen1 := int64(len(t.Command))
	if wlen := binary.PutVarint(bs, alen1); wlen >= 0 {
		wire.Write(b[0:wlen])
	}
	for i := int64(0); i < alen1; i++ {
		t.Command[i].Marshal(wire)
	}
	bs = b[:4]
	tmp32 = t.Seq
	bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	wire.Write(bs)
	bs = b[:]
	alen2 := int64(len(t.Deps))
	if wlen := binary.PutVarint(bs, alen2); wlen >= 0 {
		wire.Write(b[0:wlen])
	}
	for i := int64(0); i < alen2; i++ {
		bs = b[:4]
		tmp32 = t.Deps[i]
		bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
		bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
		bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
		bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
		wire.Write(bs)
	}
}

func (t *PrepareReply) Unmarshal(rr io.Reader) error {
	var wire byteReader
	var ok bool
	if wire, ok = rr.(byteReader); !ok {
		wire = bufio.NewReader(rr)
	}
	var b [17]byte
	var bs []byte
	bs = b[:17]
	if _, err := io.ReadAtLeast(wire, bs, 17); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.AcceptorId = int32((uint32(bs[0]) | (uint32(bs[1]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[2]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[3]) << 24)))
	t.Replica = int32((uint32(bs[4]) | (uint32(bs[5]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[6]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[7]) << 24)))
	t.Instance = int32((uint32(bs[8]) | (uint32(bs[9]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[10]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[11]) << 24)))
	t.Ballot = int32((uint32(bs[12]) | (uint32(bs[13]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[14]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[15]) << 24)))
	t.Status = int8(bs[16])
	alen1, err := binary.ReadVarint(wire)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.Command = make([]state.Command, alen1)
	for i := int64(0); i < alen1; i++ {
		t.Command[i].Unmarshal(wire)
	}
	bs = b[:4]
	if _, err := io.ReadAtLeast(wire, bs, 4); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.Seq = int32((uint32(bs[0]) | (uint32(bs[1]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[2]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[3]) << 24)))
	alen2, err := binary.ReadVarint(wire)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.Deps = make([]int32, alen2)
	for i := int64(0); i < alen2; i++ {
		if _, err := io.ReadAtLeast(wire, bs, 4); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		t.Deps[i] = int32((uint32(bs[0]) | (uint32(bs[1]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[2]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[3]) << 24)))
	}
	return nil
}

type PrepareReply struct {
	AcceptorId int32
	Replica    int32
	Instance   int32
	Ballot     int32
	VBallot    int32
	Status     int8
	Command    []state.Command
	Seq        int32
	Deps       []int32

func New(alias string, id int, peerAddrList []string, exec, beacon, durable bool, batchWait int, transconf bool, failures int, conf *config.Config, logger *dlog.Logger) *Replica {
	r := &Replica{
		replica.New(alias, id, failures, peerAddrList, true, exec, false, conf, logger),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE*3),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE*3),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE*2),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0,
		make([][]*Instance, len(peerAddrList)),
		make([]int32, len(peerAddrList)),
		make([]int32, len(peerAddrList)),
		make([]int32, len(peerAddrList)),
		nil,
		make([]map[state.Key]*InstPair, len(peerAddrList)),
		make(map[state.Key]int32),
		0,
		0,
		-1,
		new(sync.Mutex),
		make(chan *instanceId, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		false,
		-1,
		batchWait,
		transconf,
	}

	r.Beacon = beacon
	r.Durable = durable

	for i := 0; i < r.N; i++ {
		r.InstanceSpace[i] = make([]*Instance, MAX_INSTANCE) // FIXME
		r.crtInstance[i] = -1
		r.ExecedUpTo[i] = -1
		r.CommittedUpTo[i] = -1
		r.conflicts[i] = make(map[state.Key]*InstPair, HT_INIT_SIZE)
	}

	r.exec = &Exec{r}

	cpMarker = make([]state.Command, 0)

	//register RPCs
	r.prepareRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(Prepare), r.prepareChan)
	r.prepareReplyRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(PrepareReply), r.prepareReplyChan)
	r.preAcceptRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(PreAccept), r.preAcceptChan)
	r.preAcceptReplyRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(PreAcceptReply), r.preAcceptReplyChan)
	r.acceptRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(Accept), r.acceptChan)
	r.acceptReplyRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(AcceptReply), r.acceptReplyChan)
	r.commitRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(Commit), r.commitChan)
	r.tryPreAcceptRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(TryPreAccept), r.tryPreAcceptChan)
	r.tryPreAcceptReplyRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(TryPreAcceptReply), r.tryPreAcceptReplyChan)

	r.Stats.M["weird"], r.Stats.M["conflicted"], r.Stats.M["slow"], r.Stats.M["fast"], r.Stats.M["totalCommitTime"], r.Stats.M["totalBatching"], r.Stats.M["totalBatchingSize"] = 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0

	go r.run()

	return r
}

func (r *Replica) recordInstanceMetadata(inst *Instance) {
	if !r.Durable {
		return
	}

	b := make([]byte, 9+r.N*4)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[0:4], uint32(inst.bal))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[0:4], uint32(inst.vbal))
	b[4] = byte(inst.Status)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[5:9], uint32(inst.Seq))
	l := 9
	for _, dep := range inst.Deps {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[l:l+4], uint32(dep))
		l += 4
	}
	r.StableStore.Write(b[:])
}

func (r *Replica) recordCommands(cmds []state.Command) {
	if !r.Durable {
		return
	}

	if cmds == nil {
		return
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(cmds); i++ {
		cmds[i].Marshal(io.Writer(r.StableStore))
	}
}

func (r *Replica) sync() {
	if !r.Durable {
		return
	}

	r.StableStore.Sync()

formation.explanation: Client admission allocates an owner-row instance, computes dependencies and sequence from conflicts and preaccepts. Live preferred peers establish or retain local state and reply. Coordinator filters reply ballot/phase, merges attributes, and commits on fast-path predicates or sends Accept. Matching Accept replies plus self support can commit. Commit broadcasts full commands/attributes; receivers reject stale ballots or already-decided state. Execution waits for committed command-bearing dependency graph components before application and default client completion.

context.explanation: Authority is per-instance: original row ballot equals owner ID. Recipients reject below joined bal; Prepare advances bal and reports vbal/history. Incomplete execution prefixes trigger recovery. Recovery replaces bookkeeping, obtains matching-ballot replies, and selects prior state by VBallot before choosing Accept, phase-one restart, or committed installation. A leader flag changes ballot generation but does not remove every replica ability to propose. Old replies are phase/ballot filtered; pending commands can survive via recovered state/clientProposals. Already committed local state resists Accept/Commit replacement.

connection.explanation: Formation creates the stored support later reported by Prepare. Ballot transitions are therefore tied to both current promise and prior value context. Recovery consumer selects by VBallot, while remote serialization omits it and local recovery rewrites it before self-reporting: these are unresolved implementation discrepancies, not a demonstrated legal transfer of prior decisions. The accepted-state assignment gap is independent. Transport queues and recovery timers mean pending old work can overlap transitions; exact handler guards, not global FIFO, determine its effect.

items.rationale: Inspected fixed plan and harness under direct-checks/90b0c970a398426d91118919c8b2284e and current execution fd01442675f846f1a5adc7de29ea3b7d. The required relationship is the accepted local message-fidelity obligation, derived from handlePrepare reporting inst.vbal separately from joined bal and handlePrepareReply selecting prior state using VBallot. Harness does not assert that a preaccepted command must win recovery. Its bounded manual initialization reproduces fields actually used by these synchronous entries: empty instance rows, -1 frontiers, conflict maps, stats, N=3/F=1, volatile mode and cyclic preferred peers. Real handlePropose produces row 1 instance 0 PreAccept at ballot 1, decoded and consumed by actual handlePreAccept. The measured live instance prerequisite is nonnil, command-bearing and preaccepted with vbal 1. Actual startRecoveryForInstance emits Prepare ballot 3; explicit invocation replaces scanner timing, which is outside the obligation. Recipient handles this generated message and sends the response through actual SendMsg/Marshal. Writer buffers replace sockets without byte or field modification; the selected stream has exactly one PrepareReply. Reading the live inst.vbal after synchronous handlePrepare is a valid producer observation because that handler changes bal, not vbal, and directly copies inst.vbal into the response before returning. No concurrent mutation occurs. New/Unmarshal matches listener allocation and codec behavior. producer is the explicit admission alias; command_count/status prerequisite is independent of compared VBallot. acceptor/replica/instance identity uniquely pairs the sole input and result, without filtering on ballot or VBallot. Result decoding completed successfully and independently emitted the decoded field. Current output is producer vballot 1 and decoded vballot 0, with acceptor 2/row 1/instance 0, ballot 3, status 2 and command count 1 on both. The monitor compares actual result to producer.vballot; process PASS is not used as the oracle. Stop is after decode, independent of whether comparison holds. No resource lifecycle or pending message drain is needed for this synchronous codec scope. The measured mismatch corresponds to the bound codec omission and resolves the narrow preservation question. Explained alternatives (not unresolved conflicts): Ballot, status, command count and identity agree; only the checked prior-value ballot differs. Zero-valued VBallot inputs would coincide with the default and are not evidence of preservation for nonzero input. Earlier exploration restarted a NOOP, but its independent self-reply relabeling prevents codec-only causal attribution.
